#Brady Beckner Assignment 5

library(alr4)
library(caret)
library(parallel)

data(MinnLand)

# Removed all missing values
MinnLand=na.omit(MinnLand)

MinnLand$year=factor(MinnLand$year)


# Model 1: log response
M1=lm(log(acrePrice)~
        log(acres)*region+
        year*region+
        tillable+
        financing+
        crpPct,
      data=MinnLand)

summary(M1)


# Model 2: square-root response
M2=lm(sqrt(acrePrice)~
        log(acres)*region+
        year*region+
        tillable+
        financing+
        crpPct,
      data=MinnLand)

summary(M2)


# 5-Fold Cross-Validation

set.seed(1010)

Sets=createFolds(MinnLand$acrePrice,k=5,list=TRUE)

M1mae=0
M2mae=0

for(k in 1:5){
  
  TestDat=MinnLand[Sets[[k]],]
  TrainingDat=MinnLand[-Sets[[k]],]
  
  m1=lm(log(acrePrice)~
           log(acres)*region+
           year*region+
           tillable+financing+crpPct,
         data=TrainingDat)
  
  m2=lm(sqrt(acrePrice)~
           log(acres)*region+
           year*region+
           tillable+financing+crpPct,
         data=TrainingDat)
  
  p1=exp(predict(m1,newdata=TestDat))
  p2=predict(m2,newdata=TestDat)^2
  
  M1mae=M1mae+sum(abs(TestDat$acrePrice-p1))
  M2mae=M2mae+sum(abs(TestDat$acrePrice-p2))
}

M1mae/nrow(MinnLand)
M2mae/nrow(MinnLand)


# 10-Fold Cross-Validation

set.seed(1010)

Sets=createFolds(MinnLand$acrePrice,k=10,list=TRUE)

M1mae=0
M2mae=0

for(k in 1:10){
  
  TestDat=MinnLand[Sets[[k]],]
  TrainingDat=MinnLand[-Sets[[k]],]
  
  m1=lm(log(acrePrice)~
           log(acres)*region+
           year*region+
           tillable+financing+crpPct,
         data=TrainingDat)
  
  m2=lm(sqrt(acrePrice)~
           log(acres)*region+
           year*region+
           tillable+financing+crpPct,
         data=TrainingDat)
  
  p1=exp(predict(m1,newdata=TestDat))
  p2=predict(m2,newdata=TestDat)^2
  
  M1mae=M1mae+sum(abs(TestDat$acrePrice-p1))
  M2mae=M2mae+sum(abs(TestDat$acrePrice-p2))
}

M1mae/nrow(MinnLand)
M2mae/nrow(MinnLand)


#1000 Random Splits

randomSplit=function(i){
  
  set.seed(3322+i)
  
  Test=sample(1:nrow(MinnLand),
              size=round(.25*nrow(MinnLand)),
              replace=FALSE)
  
  TrainingDat=MinnLand[-Test,]
  TestDat=MinnLand[Test,]
  
  m1=lm(log(acrePrice)~
           log(acres)*region+
           year*region+
           tillable+financing+crpPct,
         data=TrainingDat)
  
  m2=lm(sqrt(acrePrice)~
           log(acres)*region+
           year*region+
           tillable+financing+crpPct,
         data=TrainingDat)
  
  p1=exp(predict(m1,newdata=TestDat))
  p2=predict(m2,newdata=TestDat)^2
  
  c(mean(abs(TestDat$acrePrice-p1)),
    mean(abs(TestDat$acrePrice-p2)))
}


# Parallel computing
cl=makeCluster(detectCores()-1)

clusterExport(cl,c("MinnLand","randomSplit"))

Results=parLapply(cl,1:1000,randomSplit)

stopCluster(cl)

Results=do.call(rbind,Results)

colnames(Results)=c("Log_MAE","Sqrt_MAE")

mean(Results[,1])
mean(Results[,2])


#Comparisons

CVresults=data.frame(
  Method=c("5-Fold","10-Fold","Random 1000"),
  Log_MAE=c(
    672.5578,
    673.4903,
    673.1929
  ),
  Sqrt_MAE=c(
    680.6813,
    680.8364,
    681.4419
  )
)

CVresults


#Two candidate models were created using log(acrePrice) and sqrt(acrePrice) as the response variables. The models were compared using 5-fold cross-validation, 10-fold cross-validation, and 1,000 random splits. The log(acrePrice) model had lower mae for all three methods: 672.56 compared to 680.68 for 5-fold, 673.49 compared to 680.84 for 10-fold, and 673.19 compared to 681.44 for the 1,000 random splits. I would select the log(acrePrice) model as the final model, and the results show that land prices are related to acreage, region, year, tillable land, financing, and CRP percentage.
